hero.title: Find the problems before the buyer’s team does
hero.lead: Right now, the buyer will know more about what’s wrong with your business than you do. Factum closes that gap first: {disciplines} specialist analytical passes over your own data room, grounded in your documents, reconciled against each other, and reviewed by a person before you see anything.
hero.footnote: Factum is pre-launch. We are taking on a limited number of pilot mandates — counted in single digits, not a rolling waitlist.

schema.title: A finding isn’t finished until it can be traced
schema.lead: The output schema requires a citation to a specific document and passage for every claim before a finding counts as finished.
schema.body: A structural constraint on the output, not a request the model can quietly under-deliver on twenty findings into a long run. We publish the contract rather than a specimen, because client work is confidential.

problem.title: The valuation conversation happens when you have the least power to fix anything
problem.lead: Most owners only find out what their business is really worth once a buyer already has the leverage. Know your number and close the gaps early, on your own terms, not the buyer’s.

points.title: Whoever finds it first frames it
points.body: Every week a data room sits without a pass like this behind it is a week the buyer’s own analysts might find something first — and whoever finds an issue first controls how it gets framed for the rest of the negotiation.

points.title: One dimension isn’t diligence
points.body: A traditional sell-side quality-of-earnings read covers one dimension. A buyer’s team will not stop at one. The gaps show up in the space between disciplines.

points.title: A risk list is not an argument
points.body: Most diligence is a static risk list — nobody actively hunts for value-creation levers. The report reads as a warning, not a reason to pay more.

points.title: A clean room still has to hold
points.body: A clean data room only pays off if it holds up across the table when the buyer’s team pushes back.

pipeline.title: A tested pipeline, not a session someone has to steer
pipeline.lead: Any competent analyst can point an agentic tool at a data room and have it genuinely work through the documents. The difference is what is engineered to happen every time versus what depends on how well the session is steered on a given day.
pipeline.refusalNote: Hard-coded, even after repeated retries. All three route to a human instead of silently passing through.

header.title: {modules} modules, and the machinery that keeps them honest
header.lead: The interesting part of an AI diligence platform isn’t that it can read a data room. It’s what is structurally required to happen before a finding is allowed to reach you.

difference.title: Engineered every time versus steered on the day
difference.lead: None of this requires believing general agentic AI is incapable. It requires recognising that a tested pipeline someone has already built, run and hardened across engagements is a different thing from assembling that same rigor yourself, correctly, under deal pressure, this one time.

points.title: A tested, repeatable methodology
points.body: Not a workflow assembled fresh each session. The coverage doesn’t depend on remembering to ask for it correctly this time.

points.title: Citations as a schema constraint
points.body: Every claim needs a specific document and passage before the finding counts as finished. A structural constraint on the output, not a request the model can quietly under-deliver on.

points.title: Cross-discipline reconciliation as a fixed step
points.body: The real value in a diligence read is catching what only shows up when the financial numbers, the corporate registry, the legal contracts and the HR records are read against each other.

points.title: A standing verification gate
points.body: A review pass that runs every time, not only when someone thinks to ask the agent to double-check itself.

pipeline.title: From upload to a finding you can act on
pipeline.lead: End to end, from data-room upload to drafted findings, the analysis step runs with no human in the loop. The one mandatory human step is a review and approval gate on findings that already exist.

stages.title: Grounded retrieval
stages.body: Each of the modules is an independent agent that retrieves grounded evidence directly from the uploaded documents, not free-generated text.
stages.note: Confidential financial and personal data is pseudonymized before it reaches this layer.

stages.title: Drafting against the schema
stages.body: The agent drafts findings inside an output schema that requires a citation to a specific document and passage for every claim.

stages.title: Generate-critique-retry
stages.body: A second reviewer agent critiques the draft and sends it back. The loop repeats before anything reaches a person.
stages.note: The platform’s own term for it: a generate-critique-retry loop.

stages.title: Independent fact-check
stages.body: A second, independent fact-checking pass cross-verifies claims against the source text, separately from the reviewer agent.
stages.note: A third checking layer, distinct from both the reviewer agent and the human gate.

stages.title: Cross-discipline reconciliation
stages.body: Every discipline’s findings are checked against every other’s and resolved into one coherent narrative before you see anything.

stages.title: Human review and approval
stages.body: A post-hoc review gate on already-generated findings. That review isn’t a formality bolted on to make AI output presentable — it’s the actual mechanism that makes machine-speed analysis safe to rely on for a decision this size.
stages.note: Pseudonymization is reversed only here, in the final delivered output.

anatomy.title: What every finding has to carry

refusals.title: Three things the loop will not auto-approve
refusals.lead: The reviewer-agent loop is hard-coded to refuse to auto-approve three failure classes even after repeated retries, routing all three to a human instead of silently passing them through.

classes.title: Fabricated or hallucinated source citations
classes.body: A citation that does not resolve to a real passage in a real uploaded document stops the finding.

classes.title: Privacy leaks
classes.body: Material that should not have crossed into the analysis layer, or out of it, is routed to a person rather than released.

classes.title: Scope refusals
classes.body: Where a module cannot answer within its brief, it says so and escalates instead of producing something adjacent.

limits.title: What we don’t claim about the platform
limits.lead: Being specific about the boundary is part of the product. Everything on this page describes a mechanism; none of it is a certified metric.
items: No accuracy rate. The pipeline’s internal benchmarks are single-dataset, internal and unaudited, so they are not published here as a headline number.
No claim that the human gate is optional. It is mandatory, and the analysis is not a finished product without it.
No completed public case studies. The first ones are ahead of us, not behind us.

No claim that every layer has the same track record. The financial module has been run end to end on a live deal and independently verified against source documents; the newest reconciliation layer is younger than that.
No general availability. Factum is pre-launch.

items.q: Isn’t this just an AI chatbot with extra steps?
items.a: No — and to be precise about it, since modern agentic AI genuinely can do multi-step, tool-using work, not just chat. The difference isn’t AI versus no AI; it’s a tested, repeatable pipeline versus a session someone has to steer correctly, live, under deal pressure. Every discipline runs as its own pre-scoped pass against the full document set, every time, and the cross-check between them is a fixed step rather than something an operator has to remember to ask for.

items.q: How do I know the platform can carry findings this material?
items.a: The financial module — the most numerically exposed part of any diligence read — has already been run end to end on a live deal and independently verified against source documents. Newer layers have less history behind them, and we will tell you which is which on your engagement rather than let the strongest claim cover the whole system.

items.q: What happens when the model doesn’t know?
items.a: It has to say so. A finding is either backed by a real citation or explicitly flagged as unconfirmed. What it cannot do is invent the difference — an unresolvable citation is one of the three failure classes the reviewer loop refuses to auto-approve.

items.q: Who is accountable for what reaches me?
items.a: A named person, who reviews every output before it leaves. Not routed through a black box with no one to ask.

The pipeline pass across every discipline runs in hours rather than the weeks a traditional multi-advisor process takes, and the finished, reviewed output is produced in days, not weeks. We don’t quote a guaranteed delivery date before seeing the data room.

faq.title: The ones that come up first

items.q: Does this replace a quality-of-earnings report?
items.a: It is broader, and it is not an attest service. A traditional sell-side quality-of-earnings read covers one dimension and takes four to ten weeks; this runs eleven disciplines and reconciles them against each other. Where your process needs a signed accountant’s opinion, that stays a separate engagement with a separate firm.

A full eleven-discipline pass is produced in days, not weeks. The pipeline pass itself runs in hours; the human review and the reconciliation sit after it. We don’t commit to a date before seeing the data room.

A single price for the whole scope rather than a tiered menu, set on the intake call against the size and state of your data room. A tiered scope-upsell structure is a tool for extracting more from bigger-budget buyers, which isn’t the objective on a first engagement.

Confidential financial and personal data is pseudonymized before it reaches the analysis layer and reversed only in the final delivered output. All analysis runs on Google Vertex AI in an EU region under a Data Processing Agreement, and the model provider does not retain your documents or use them for training beyond the processing call. The governance page sets out both what that covers and what it doesn’t.

items.q: Can I see an example report?
items.a: Not a real one. Client documents are confidential and no client has elected to be named, so there is no anonymised extract we’re willing to publish. What we can show you on a call is the live dashboard, the output schema every finding has to satisfy, and how a finding traces back to its source passage.
A named person, before anything reaches your desk. Not routed through a black box with no one to ask. While Factum is pre-launch that person is the founder, on every mandate.

cta.body: The intake call is a scoping conversation: what’s in the room, what’s missing, and whether a sprint is the right instrument for where you are.

header.title: How your documents are handled, and what we don’t claim
header.lead: Data handling isn’t an afterthought bolted on to satisfy a checkbox — it’s built into how the pipeline runs. It is also narrower than most security pages imply, so this one states the boundary explicitly.

data.title: Four things that are true of every engagement
data.lead: Each of these describes a mechanism in the pipeline. None of them is a certification, and we don’t present them as one.

gate.title: The one mandatory human step
gate.lead: End to end, the analysis runs without a human in the loop. The gate sits after it, on findings that already exist, and it is not optional.
items: Findings are checked back against the source documents before delivery.
The gate runs every time, not only when someone thinks to ask the system to double-check itself.
Three failure classes are hard-coded to route to a person rather than auto-approve: fabricated or hallucinated source citations, privacy leaks, and scope refusals.
A named person reviews, reconciles and stands behind the output before it leaves.
Pseudonymized values are reversed only here, in the final delivered output — not in any intermediate step.

transparency.title: Where the machine ends and a person starts
transparency.lead: You should be able to tell, for any finding, what produced it and what checked it.
transparency.body: The analysis is generated by independent agents that retrieve evidence from your own uploaded documents. A second reviewer agent critiques each draft in a generate-critique-retry loop, and a separate fact-checking pass cross-verifies claims against the source text. A person then reviews the result before it reaches you. If a claim cannot be tied to a passage in a real document, the output is required to flag it as unconfirmed rather than present it as established.

limits.title: What we don’t claim
limits.lead: Most of what a buyer would want on a page like this, we don’t have yet. Listing it is more useful to you than implying it.
items: No ISO 27001, SOC 2 or any other certification, and no third-party audit of the pipeline.
No penetration test, sub-processor list, single sign-on or audit-log commitment.
No published EU region. Analysis runs on Google Vertex AI in an EU region; we don’t name a specific one.
No retention or deletion period committed on Factum’s own side. Zero retention is the model provider’s commitment, not a description of our storage.
No asserted GDPR-compliance status. Specific processing terms belong in an engagement agreement, not on a marketing page.
No professional-indemnity cover, breach-notification commitment or disaster-recovery arrangement stated here.
limits.note: If your process requires any of the above in writing, raise it on the intake call. There is a real answer either way, and a short one.

header.title: Judgment, not just software
header.lead: Two vantage points on one problem: a banker’s read on risk, and an engineer’s discipline for systems that don’t break.

people.name: Wouter Dijkman
people.title: Founder, Factum
people.bio: More than five years inside the institutions that fund these deals. At ING, Wouter worked Acquisition & Leveraged Finance, structuring and vetting the credit behind exactly this kind of transaction. Before that, at Rabobank, he specialized in financial restructuring, reading a company’s numbers for what they actually mean rather than what they’re presented to mean. He also runs Agentic Mindshift, his own AI consultancy, so the AI-driven diligence work isn’t a banker’s side project. He founded Factum to bring that same scrutiny to the sell side, so an owner walks into their exit with the rigor a bank would apply, before a buyer gets the chance to use it against them.

people.name: Daniel Dropuljic
people.title: Technical Lead, Factum
people.bio: Daniel builds the systems behind Factum’s AI-driven diligence work. As founder of Dandro Solutions, he designs data pipelines processing over 50,000 records a day for international healthcare clients, under strict compliance regimes including GDPR and FHIR. That discipline — production-grade, auditable, built to hold up under scrutiny — is what Factum’s diligence engine runs on.

history.role: HL7/FHIR implementation, led a three-person team

team.closing: A banker’s read on risk and an engineer’s discipline for systems that don’t break. Together they back the process with judgment, not just software.

boundaries.title: What a partnership does not include
boundaries.lead: Some of these are commitments to existing partners. The rest is just the honest state of a pre-launch company.
items: No white-labelled claim of certification or audit. We can stand behind the mechanism, not behind a badge we don’t hold.
No unlimited capacity. Factum is pre-launch and delivery is deliberately small; a partnership that outruns the review gate is worse than no partnership.
No blanket referral-fee policy. Where attest or independence rules apply, that is checked per relationship and disclosed to the client.
No claim on your client. The relationship is yours, and nothing we run for you becomes a reference or a case study without your written agreement.
No conflicting mandate in a lane we have already committed exclusively. Where an exclusivity exists we will say so, rather than quietly work around it.

items.q: Do you work directly with owners as well?

items.q: Whose name goes on the report?

items.q: Can you run only part of the scope?
items.a: The eleven-discipline pass is a fixed step, because the value is in the reconciliation between disciplines rather than in any one of them. What can vary is the depth of the write-up and which findings you want surfaced to the client.
Exclusivity is possible in a defined lane, and it is a real commitment when we make it. What we won’t do is imply exclusivity we haven’t agreed, in either direction.

sections.title: Documents you share with us
body: No documents are shared through this website. Document access is agreed separately, in writing, before anything is transferred.

During an engagement, confidential financial and personal data is pseudonymized before it reaches the analysis layer, and reversed only in the final delivered output. Analysis runs on Google Vertex AI in an EU region under a Data Processing Agreement; the model provider does not retain your documents or use them for model training beyond the processing call itself.
Retention, deletion and confidentiality terms on our own side are set in the engagement agreement rather than asserted here.

sections.title: Your rights
body: Under the GDPR you can ask what personal data we hold about you, ask for it to be corrected, ask for it to be deleted, or object to how it is used. Raise it on the intake call or reply to any email from us, and you will get an answer.
If you are not satisfied with how we handle a request, you can complain to the Dutch data protection authority, the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens.

sections.title: Changes
body: This page will change as Factum moves out of pre-launch and the engagement terms firm up. The review date at the top is the honest signal of how current it is.
